summary: The paper investigates confidence-based and execution-filtered routing between Qwen2.5-1.5B and Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B on semantic Python repair problems. The benchmark rigorously demonstrates that while an oracle routing policy reveals strong complementary error potential (268 solves out of 512), empirical confidence routing and cascading fail to surpass standalone models or simple execution-based filtering.
strengths: Rigorous experimental control with pre-specified validation thresholds, split discovery/validation/test workflows, and 5,000 bootstrap resamples for paired confidence intervals.
Transparent presentation of negative empirical results, effectively exposing the substantial gap between oracle potential and realistic confidence-based routing.
Counterfactual paired problem design that isolates whether model predictions genuinely adapt to requested specification changes.
Comprehensive documentation of hyperparameters, seeds, and reproduction commands for independent verification.
weaknesses: Evaluation domain relies on a synthetic toy puzzle (variable assignment and swapping) rather than naturalistic, complex software engineering tasks.
Resource efficiency is reported solely via forward-pass count without profiling actual inference latency, memory overhead, or end-to-end wall-clock time.
Submitted under text_only track without a formally attached repository artifact in the platform metadata.
suggestions: Extend the routing and execution-filtering benchmark to natural code datasets such as HumanEval-Infill or SWE-bench Lite.
Profile actual wall-clock execution and memory footprints across different deployment environments alongside token forward-pass counts.
Test additional routing signals, such as model entropy or token-level logit temperature scaling, beyond top-two logit margin.

claims.text: Infill pretraining supplies the two-sided code interface.
Functional tests and the strength of test suites are established concerns in language-model code evaluation.
We compared the original pinned Qwen2.5-1.5B base host and Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B base donor.

novelty_vs_existing.contribution: Applies standard fill-in-the-middle prompting paradigms specifically to benchmark model cascading and execution-guided reranking between heterogeneous model sizes.

novelty_vs_existing.title: Qwen2.5-Coder Technical Report
novelty_vs_existing.contribution: Evaluates complementary error distribution and routing efficiency between small coder models and base host models on semantic repair tasks.

novelty_vs_existing.title: Is Your Code Generated by ChatGPT Really Correct? Rigorous Evaluation of Large Language Models for Code Generation
novelty_vs_existing.contribution: Examines ambiguous visible test executions as dynamic routing signals in a multi-model pipeline rather than relying on comprehensive offline test augmentation.
